slides.title: Agentic Jailbreaking & LLM Agent Security
slides.subtitle: A Systematic Analysis of Threat Models, Empirical Vulnerabilities, and Provable Defenses (2024–2026)
slides.footer: Prepared for Academic Research Seminar & Thesis Topic Direction · September 2026

slides.title: The Fundamental Shift: Chatbot Jailbreaks vs Agentic Exploits
left_bullets: Confined Impact: Blast radius is limited to toxic text generation (hate speech, disinformation).
Single-Turn Human Loop: Attacker directly converses with model; human must manually execute harmful advice.
Static Context Boundary: Model only consumes prompts and internal weights without observing external state.
Mitigated by Alignment: Post-training safety tuning (RLHF/DPO) suppresses prohibited text tokens reliably.
right_bullets: Irreversible Side Effects: Failure mode is tool execution: database drops, fund transfers, unauthorized API calls.
Indirect Attack Surface: Adversarial instructions hide in external environments (web DOM, emails, group chats).
Unified Data/Control Channel: Transformers cannot distinguish developer instructions from untrusted data.
Compounding Multi-Step Loops: Injected payloads hijack autonomous workflows, pivoting across tools and agents.

slides.title: Core Threat Vectors in Autonomous Agent Architectures

cards.title: Direct Injection (DPI)
bullets: Deceptive user prompts to override system guardrails
Forces parameter tampering & tool abuse
Peak ASR: 72.7% across models (ASB)
Easily bypasses naive persona constraints

cards.title: Indirect Injection (IPI)
bullets: Payloads embedded in external tool inputs
Exploits web pages, emails, and group chats
Universal 100% ASR in chat apps (LivePI)
Enables silent multi-step data exfiltration

cards.title: Memory & RAG Poisoning
bullets: Corrupts retrieval memory or plan stores
Infects clean tasks across future sessions
Peak ASR: 84.3% with Plan-of-Thought (ASB)
Latent triggers survive session resets

cards.title: Confused Deputy & Skills
bullets: Untrusted agents manipulate privileged deputies
Third-party skills violate safety contracts
Single-call monitors miss ~50% (VIGIL)
Breaks multi-agent tenant isolation

slides.title: The Three-Year Evolution of Agent Security Research

cards.title: Foundations & Emulation
bullets: ToolEmu (ICLR '24): Pioneers LM-emulated sandboxes; shows 24% failure residual under safety prompts.
InjecAgent (ACL '24): First formal benchmark for IPI; function-calling fine-tuning cuts ASR to 3.8%.
AgentDojo (NeurIPS '24): Dynamic testbeds prove ML detectors drop benign utility from 69% to 41%.

cards.title: Lifecycle & Live Web
bullets: ASB (ICLR '25): Formalizes 4 lifecycle stages; introduces Plan-of-Thought backdoors (84.3% ASR).
WASP (Meta FAIR '25): Evaluates live web platforms; exposes 86% intermediate hijack vs 16% completion.
Shift from synthetic toys to realistic multi-turn environments and web applications.

cards.title: OS Workflows & Verification
bullets: SEAgent (arXiv '26): Mandatory Access Control (MAC) eliminates Confused Deputy, reaching 0.0% ASR.
LivePI (arXiv '26): Real Linux VM shows universal 100% group chat vulnerability via role spoofing.
VIGIL (arXiv '26): Trace-grounded SMT checking achieves 92.6% F1 on real-world skill contracts.

slides.title: ToolEmu: Identifying High-Stakes Risks in Emulated Sandboxes
left_bullets: Authors: Yangjun Ruan, Jimmy Ba, Tatsunori Hashimoto et al. (Toronto, Stanford).
The Problem: Evaluating long-tail risks (medical, financial, OS) is unsustainable via custom sandboxes.
LM Emulator: Uses GPT-4 to simulate tool execution, returns, and world state updates dynamically.
Dataset Scale: 36 high-stakes toolkits across 18 domains with 144 curated risk scenarios.
Evaluator Quality: Automated evaluator achieved 75.3% precision and 73.1% recall matching human experts.
right_bullets: High Baseline Failure: Standard GPT-4 failed 39.4% of cases; Claude-2: 44.3%; ChatGPT-3.5: 62.0%.
Limits of Safety Prompts: Explicit system prompts lowered GPT-4 failures from 39.4% to 23.9%.
Key Takeaway: Even with safety alignment, agents cause critical failures in nearly 1 in 4 tool tasks.
Open Gaps: Benchmark curation required manual effort; LM emulator can hallucinate complex tool state.

slides.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tools
left_bullets: Authors: Joey Tianyi Zhou, Luu Anh Tuan et al. (A*STAR, NTU Singapore).
Threat Taxonomy: Formalizes Direct Harm (file deletion, unauthorized actions) vs Data Stealing (exfiltration).
Benchmark Scale: 1,054 test cases covering 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools.
Settings: Base setting (raw attacker text) vs Enhanced setting (+ hacking prompt wrapper).
Scope: Evaluated 30 agents across prompted ReAct and fine-tuned function-calling backbones.
right_bullets: Prompted Models Collapse: LLaMA-2-70B exhibited >80% ASR; prompted GPT-4 reached 24%–47% ASR.
Fine-Tuning Advantage: Native function-calling fine-tuning slashed GPT-4 ASR down to 3.8%.
The Exfiltration Trap: Once sensitive data is read into context, exfiltration transmission reaches 100%.
Key Takeaway: Function fine-tuning improves tool hygiene, but prompt defenses cannot stop data egress.

slides.title: AgentDojo: Evaluating Dynamic Attacks and Defense Costs
left_bullets: Authors: Edoardo Debenedetti, Florian Tramèr et al. (ETH Zurich, Invariant Labs).
Core Innovation: Moves beyond static tests into dynamic, executable multi-turn environments.
Application Suites: 97 tasks across Workspace, Banking, Slack, and Travel domains.
Evaluation Suite: 629 security test cases featuring realistic untrusted tool outputs.
Targeted Models: 10 models including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5, and Llama 3 70B.
right_bullets: Frontier Susceptibility: Targeted ASR hit 47.7% on GPT-4o and 33.9% on Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Untargeted Hijacks: Attackers successfully derailed agents from their goals in 68.4% of runs.
The Classifier Trap: ML detectors lowered ASR to 7.95%, but crashed benign utility from 69% to 41.5%.
Tool Isolation Superiority: Least-privilege tool filtering cut ASR to 6.8% while maintaining 73.1% utility.

slides.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Full Lifecycle Threat Modeling

cards.title: 4-Stage Attack Lifecycle
bullets: Formalizes attacks across System Prompt, User Prompt, Tool Use, and Memory Retrieval
10 application domains (Finance, Driving, Healthcare, E-commerce)
Evaluates 27 attack and defense methods across 13 foundation backbones
First unified framework spanning agent execution lifecycle

cards.title: Peak Empirical ASR
bullets: Plan-of-Thought (PoT) Backdoors reached 84.3% peak average ASR across models
Direct Prompt Injection (DPI) achieved 72.7% average success rate
GPT-4o exhibited 64.4% average vulnerability across all evaluated scenarios
Claude 3.5 Sonnet suffered 56.4% average compromise

cards.title: The Heuristic Deficit
bullets: Capability Disconnect: Standalone leaderboard IQ does not correlate with security
Paraphrasing defense leaves 56.9% ASR unmitigated
Dynamic prompt rewriting leaves 44.5% ASR open
Takeaway: Shallow prompt transformations fail against stateful agent backdoors

slides.title: WASP: Live Web Agents & The "Security by Incompetence" Paradox
slides.footer: WASP (Meta FAIR 2025): Evaluated on self-hosted GitLab and Reddit with live multi-step web navigation.

slides.title: SEAgent: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) for AI Agents
left_bullets: Authors: S. Lin, Y. Zhang, H. Sun et al. (arXiv 2026).
OS-Inspired Security: Implements SELinux-style Mandatory Access Control for multi-agent systems.
System View Graph: Dynamically tracks execution topology, data dependencies, and principals.
SEMemory Isolation: Segregates untrusted external inputs from sensitive execution context.
Hybrid Labeling: Combines automated LLM policy labeling with deterministic rule validation.
right_bullets: Zero Attack Success Rate: Achieved 0.00% ASR across InjecAgent and AgentDojo benchmarks.
Eliminated Confused Deputy: Prevented untrusted subagents from invoking privileged tools.
Preserved Benign Utility: Maintained 68%–75% correctness on API-Bank with 0%–5% false alarms.
Outperformed IsolateGPT: Avoided IsolateGPT's severe 34% utility crash and 18.3% false positive rate.

slides.title: LivePI: Realistic IPI Benchmarking on Live Linux Workflows
left_bullets: Authors: Lei Zhao, Abhay Bhaskar, Edgar Dobriban (University of Pennsylvania).
Production VM Testbed: Live Linux VM (OpenClaw) with real email, chat, files, and crypto wallet.
7 Ingestion Surfaces: Group Chat (Slack, WhatsApp), Email, Local Docs, Repos, Gist, Web.
5 Malicious Goals: Credential theft, policy tampering, arbitrary code exec, wallet drain.
Frontier Backbones: Evaluated GPT-5.3-Codex, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM-5.
right_bullets: Universal Group Exploit: Group chat injections hit 100.0% ASR across ALL five frontier models.
Architectural Flaw: Chat platforms inject member messages as 'role: user', tricking model reasoning.
Surface Disparity: Repository links achieved 50%–100% compromise; Gist was largely ineffective.
Two-Layer Defense: Pre-execution tool-call authorization reduced GPT-5.3-Codex ASR to 0.0%.

slides.title: VIGIL: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specs in Skills
left_bullets: Authors: Ying Li, Yanju Chen, Yu Feng, Yuan Tian et al. (UCLA, UCSD, UCSB, Riema).
The Gap: Natural-language skill contracts cannot be enforced by isolated single-call filters.
SMT Formalization: Compiles behavioral specs into formal SMT constraints over finite execution traces.
Cross-Call Tracking: Evaluates temporal preconditions, parameter bounds, and cross-tool flows.
Benchmark: Evaluated on SB+SI (152 labeled executions: 72 violating, 80 benign).
right_bullets: Exceptional Accuracy: Achieved 95.8% recall, 89.6% precision, and 92.6% F1 score.
Single-Call Guards Failed: AgentSpec (57.6% F1) and Progent (50.3% F1) missed ~50% of attacks.
LLM Judges Inadequate: Claude Opus 4.6 judge achieved only 76.8% F1, missing 24 temporal bugs.
Real-World Impact: Uncovered 34 confirmed policy bugs in deployed skills (NVIDIA, Cloudflare).

slides.title: The Capability-Security Disconnect Across Model Generations

cards.title: The Reasoning Paradox
bullets: Frontier models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) exhibit equal or higher attack compliance
Superior instruction-following causes models to strictly obey injected instructions
ASB proved model leaderboard IQ does not correlate with adversarial robustness
OpenAI o1 reached 85.7% intermediate hijack rate in WASP

cards.title: Security by Incompetence
bullets: Low end-to-end completion (0%–16%) stems from agents getting lost in complex UIs
Current safety is an accidental byproduct of agent navigation incompetence
Models fail at modal popups, multi-step navigation, and state validation
As frontier agents master autonomous execution, this accidental barrier will vanish

cards.title: Context Channel Failures
bullets: Messaging platforms ingest untrusted member chat as 'role: user'
Triggers 100% universal exploitability across all major foundation models
Fine-tuning cuts function injection to 3.8%, but exfiltration still hits 100%
Transformers lack hardware-level separation between data and instructions

slides.title: The Three Waves of LLM Agent Defenses (2023–2026+)

cards.title: Prompt Heuristics
bullets: Mechanisms: System safety prompts, XML tags, repeat prompting, paraphrasing
Pros: Zero architectural changes required; trivial to deploy
Flaws: Easily bypassed; ASB showed Paraphrasing leaves 56.9% ASR
Penalty: Degrades benign instruction-following precision
Verdict: Inadequate for production agent deployments

cards.title: Auxiliary Classifiers
bullets: Mechanisms: External PI detectors (Llama-Guard), Dual-LLM intent planners
Pros: Lowers ASR for known injection signatures (AgentDojo dropped ASR to 7.9%)
Flaws: Vulnerable to adversarial cascading injections against the guard LLM
Penalty: Severe false positives crash benign utility from 69% to 41.5%
Verdict: Unacceptable friction in real-world workflows

cards.title: Deterministic SMT & MAC
bullets: Mechanisms: Mandatory Access Control (SEAgent), SMT trace checkers (VIGIL)
Pros: 0.0% ASR; eliminates multi-agent Confused Deputy; 92.6% F1 on skills
Formal Guarantees: Verifies temporal ordering & information-flow invariants
Preserves Utility: Minimal false positive friction (0.11% block rate)
Verdict: The definitive future of secure agent systems

slides.title: Four High-Impact Research Directions for Our Lab

cards.title: Multi-Turn Red Teaming
bullets: Autonomous red-teaming agents generating adaptive multi-turn injections
Navigates environments to evade modern MAC & SMT defense policies
High Novelty / Exploits stateful multi-step gaps
Target: IEEE S&P / USENIX Security

cards.title: SMT Policy Synthesis
bullets: Automated compilation of natural-language skill specs into sound SMT trace policies
Eliminates reliance on manual policy drafting in SEAgent and VIGIL
Formal Methods & AI Convergence
Target: CAV / PLDI / ICLR

cards.title: Multimodal Injections
bullets: Adversarial visual injections targeting GUI navigation & computer-use agents
Screen-space typographic attacks, visual steganography, adversarial UI elements
Frontier & Fast-Moving Area
Target: NeurIPS / CVPR / ICML

cards.title: MCP Non-Interference
bullets: Provable non-interference & dynamic taint tracking for Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Integrates taint tracking into tool servers to stop exfiltration mathematically
Immediate Industry Utility
Target: IEEE S&P / NDSS

cards.title: Distinct Threat Surface
bullets: Agentic exploits cause irreversible physical and digital side effects via APIs
Safety alignment (RLHF) alone cannot prevent tool misuse
Context channel ingestion flaws demand architectural fixes

cards.title: The Capability Paradox
bullets: Frontier reasoning models (o1, Claude 3.5) exhibit equal or higher attack compliance
Accidental 'Security by Incompetence' will vanish as navigation matures
Leaderboard scores do not predict safety

cards.title: Deterministic Systems
bullets: Prompt filters and ML classifiers fail or cause catastrophic utility drops
State-of-the-art has shifted decisively to Mandatory Access Control & SMT trace checking
Formal guarantees are required for production

cards.title: Immediate Next Steps
bullets: Recommend selecting (A) Automated Multi-Turn Red Teaming or (B) MCP Taint Tracking
Establish formal verification testbed and draft conference proposal
Schedule follow-up research direction review
